meta.title: The potential adverse effects of hypodermic glucagon-like peptide -1 receptor agonist on patients with type 2 diabetes: A population-based study.
meta.abstract:
Background

Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs), a class of injectable antidiabetic drugs, have shown significant efficacies in improving glycemic and weight control in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2D). However, the long-term safety of GLP-1 RAs remains insufficiently studied. This study aimed to provide real-world evidence on potential adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use in T2D patients without major chronic diseases including impaired cardiac or renal function.

Methods

We conducted a retrospective cohort study involving 7746 T2D patients on GLP-1 RAs in Shenzhen, China. They were compared with 124 371 metformin-only users and 36 146 insulin-only users, forming two therapy control groups. GLP-1 RAs users were also further 1:2 paired with the control groups. Competing risk survival analyses were conducted to assess the incidence risks, presenting subdistributional hazard ratios (sHRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) for various adverse outcomes associated with GLP-1 RAs use.

Results

Compared with metformin-only users, GLP-1 RAs use was associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes (sHRs with 95% CIs), including pancreatitis (2.01, 1.24-3.24), acute nephritis (3.20, 2.17-4.70), kidney failure (3.73, 2.74-5.08), thyroid cancer (2.25, 1.23-4.10), and thyroid dysfunction (1.27, 1.00-1.63), respectively; Similar results were also found when compared with insulin-only users. Importantly, long-term (≥12 months) GLP-1 RAs use may further elevate the incidence risks of pancreatitis, acute nephritis, thyroid cancer, and thyroid dysfunction.

Conclusion

Compared with traditional T2D treatments, GLP-1 RAs use may be associated with increased risks of various adverse outcomes in a Chinese population. Cautions were strongly warranted in the use of GLP-1 RAs. Further validation is crucial across diverse populations.

domains.name: Confounding
domains.direction_justification: Before matching, GLP-1 RA users had higher obesity rates (BMI 30.0-39.9 kg/m2: 13.21% vs 4.87% in metformin users and 3.04% in insulin users; Table 3S), which predisposes to pancreatitis, renal disease, and cancer. Crucial confounders were either not measured or had severe missingness (HbA1c missing >90%, BMI missing ~33%), leaving substantial residual confounding that inflates risk estimates away from the null.

findings.mechanism: HbA1c was missing in 91.27% of matched participants and FPG was missing in 33.22%, preventing adequate adjustment for glycemic severity and diabetes progression.

FPG missing rate 33.22% in matched population (Table 1 footnote)

evidence: BMI unspecified: 33.81% in GLP-1 RA vs 36.08% in insulin and 32.49% vs 32.71% in metformin (Table 1)

domains.name: Measurement of the exposure
domains.direction_justification: Exposure was determined via electronic health system prescription records; non-adherence or primary non-compliance in real-world outpatient settings would introduce non-differential misclassification of exposure duration, attenuating true pharmacological effects towards the null.

findings.title: Objective prescription records utilized
findings.mechanism: Prescription coverage was tracked longitudinally across registered health institutions in Shenzhen.
evidence: GLP-1 RA group defined by cumulative prescription coverage in Health Information Database from 2016 to 2022

findings.title: Post-baseline exposure classification and immortal time bias
findings.mechanism: Classifying exposure based on cumulative therapy from baseline through the entire follow-up period conditions cohort entry on future treatment patterns and survival.
evidence: The GLP-1 RAs group was defined as any T2D patients who mainly prescribed GLP-1 RAs lasting from the baseline date to the last follow-up while the accumulative prescription period of any other antidiabetic medication <6 months.

findings.title: Absence of lag period for latent outcomes
findings.mechanism: Outcomes like thyroid cancer and leukemia were counted starting immediately from cohort entry without a lag window, capturing undiagnosed pre-existing disease brought to light by initiating new treatment.
evidence: All incidence duration/survival times for outcomes of interest were operationalized as the number of months from the initial outpatient date at baseline to the occurrence of the first recorded hospitalization/outpatient events, whichever came first.

findings.title: No washout period reported
findings.mechanism: Without a prior lookback/washout period to ensure incident, new-user status, prevalent users are mixed with incident users, confounding initial baseline risk.
evidence: Data of this study population originated from the Health Information Database of Shenzhen city in China, from the date of the first medical record included on January 1, 2016 to the last database update on September 1, 2022.

domains.name: Selection of participants into the study
domains.direction_justification: Exclusion of patients who switched or added therapies (<6 months cumulative other antidiabetic prescriptions across the entire follow-up) selects for long-term tolerant continuous users vs discontinuers, conditioning on post-baseline survival and treatment trajectories, exaggerating relative risk differences.

findings.title: Conditioning on post-baseline treatment persistence
findings.mechanism: Cohort eligibility required participants to maintain monotherapy/predominant therapy throughout follow-up (other antidiabetic prescriptions <6 months from baseline to last follow-up), creating selection bias and immortal time/continuation artifacts.
evidence: Participants restricted to those whose accumulative prescription period of any other antidiabetic medication was <6 months across entire follow-up (Section 2.1)

findings.title: Massive exclusion of eligible population
findings.mechanism: Over 362,000 patients were excluded for missing prescription data and 177,381 for missing IDs out of 985,278 candidates without evaluation of whether exclusions differed by clinical severity.
evidence: 177,381 excluded for missing IDs and 362,035 excluded for missing prescription data (Figure 1)

domains.name: Post-exposure interventions
domains.direction_justification: Treating transient side effects (e.g., nausea, vomiting, dizziness) as competing events in survival models removes individuals experiencing early side effects from subsequent risk sets for major chronic outcomes, which can distort the hazard rates in unpredictable directions.

findings.title: Competing risk definition based on minor side effects
findings.mechanism: Acute symptoms like diarrhea, acne, and dizziness were modeled as competing risks terminating time at risk.
evidence: Potential competing events defined as a binomial variable activated by diarrhea/emesis, dermatitis tetter, acne, dizziness, arrhythmia (Section 2.3)

domains.name: Missing data
domains.direction_justification: Over 90% missingness in HbA1c (91.27% in Table 1) and ~33% in BMI and FPG precludes meaningful adjustment or imputation of the strongest clinical predictors of diabetic complications and metabolic outcomes.

findings.title: Critical laboratory variables predominantly missing
findings.mechanism: Missingness was handled by creating an 'unspecified' category rather than valid imputation or complete-case sensitivity analyses, allowing unmeasured confounding to persist.
evidence: HbA1c missing rate: 90.52% in GLP-1 RAs, 91.79% in insulin, 90.45% in metformin (Table 3S footnote)
BMI missing rate: 32.31% in GLP-1 RAs, 32.78% in insulin, 24.01% in metformin (Table 3S)

domains.name: Measurement of the outcome
domains.direction_justification: Surveillance and diagnostic workup bias: patients prescribed novel injectable agents like GLP-1 RAs with known black-box warnings and GI symptoms undergo more frequent thyroid ultrasounds, serum lipase/amylase testing, and renal panels than patients on stable generic metformin, inflating detection of subclinical thyroid cancer (sHR 2.25), thyroid dysfunction (sHR 1.27), and acute pancreatitis (sHR 2.01).

findings.title: Surveillance and ascertainment bias for labeled adverse events
findings.mechanism: Outcomes were identified via ICD-10 and keyword matching in EHR without adjudication or standardized screening intervals across comparator arms, leading to higher detection rates in closely monitored GLP-1 RA patients.
evidence: Outcomes identified by ICD-10 codes, discharge diagnoses, imaging diagnoses, and regular expressions in outpatient/hospitalization texts (Table 2S)
Marked elevation in highly screen-sensitive outcomes: thyroid cancer sHR 2.25 (95% CI 1.23-4.10) and thyroid dysfunction sHR 1.27 (95% CI 1.00-1.63) vs metformin

domains.name: Selection of the reported result
domains.direction_justification: Multiple testing of dozens of secondary outcomes (e.g. leukemia sHR 15.09, 95% CI 4.65-48.98) across drug sub-types and durations without pre-specified registered analytical protocols increases the likelihood of reporting extreme spuriously elevated hazard ratios.

findings.title: Multiple testing across multiple disease endpoints and sub-agents
findings.mechanism: Numerous disease endpoints across six organ systems were tested simultaneously without adjustment for multiple comparisons.
evidence: Leukemia reported with sHR 15.09 (95% CI 4.65-48.98) after >=12 months GLP-1 RA usage vs metformin, acknowledged as a sparse-event finding

overall.summary: The study possesses a high risk of bias driven by severe unmeasured confounding (HbA1c missing in >90% of participants, BMI missing in ~33%), selection bias from defining cohorts based on longitudinal treatment continuation over entire follow-up, and diagnostic/surveillance bias where patients on GLP-1 RAs receive greater clinical monitoring and diagnostic workup for thyroid, renal, and pancreatic symptoms. These biases systematically push effect estimates away from the null, creating spurious associations with diverse adverse outcomes such as thyroid cancer, renal failure, and leukemia.

unresolvable_without_more_data: Exact raw event counts and person-time per outcome in each propensity-matched cohort (figures provide only hazard ratios and confidence intervals)
Completeness and values of missing clinical parameters (HbA1c, baseline eGFR, microalbuminuria, exact BMI)
Frequency of diagnostic imaging (e.g., thyroid ultrasound, pancreatic imaging) across treatment groups to quantify surveillance bias

baseline_comparability.summary: At baseline, GLP-1 RA users had significantly higher obesity rates (BMI 30-39.9: 13.21% vs 4.87% in metformin) and higher insurance coverage (75.60% vs 54.96%), predisposing them to both higher true risk and increased diagnostic surveillance for adverse outcomes. Key clinical confounders including baseline eGFR, proteinuria, and diabetes duration were unmeasured, and HbA1c was missing for over 90% of participants.

time_related_biases.summary: The study defines exposure groups based on predominant treatment patterns across the entirety of follow-up rather than at cohort entry, introducing immortal time bias and prevalent-user selection. Furthermore, no lag period was applied for chronic outcomes such as thyroid cancer and leukemia despite a mean follow-up of only ~24 months, heavily biasing risk estimates away from the null through surveillance and reverse causation.
